tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your Monday September 21st market briefing.

Futures are rallying to start the week. The S&P is up about 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq is up 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 is up 47 basis points. Asia closed broadly higher — Hang Seng up over one percent, Korea up one point six five percent, and most other markets up around one percent. European indices are up 85 to 120 basis points with data center pick-and-shovel stocks leading.

Here is what makes this morning interesting — almost all of the weekend news was negative, yet futures are green. The reason seems to be one thing: diplomatic optimism around the United Nations General Assembly, which runs this week in New York. Trump signaled he would be open to meeting with Iran's president, and reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Markets are betting that even a small improvement in Middle East tensions could knock oil lower, and if oil falls sustainably, the knock-on effects are significant — lower yields, less hawkish Fed policy, better margins, improved consumer confidence. That is the entire bull case in a nutshell.

On rates, Treasuries have a bid with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. The Fed remains in hawkish mode — the market is pricing roughly 33 basis points of additional hikes across the final two meetings of the year, with about 50/50 odds on the October 28th meeting. Kansas City Fed's Schmid and Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari both warned over the weekend that inflation is running hot beyond just oil prices. Treasury also plans to issue over one trillion dollars in T-bills over the next 12 months, pushing short-term debt above 24 percent of marketable debt — above the Treasury's own 20 percent target.

Now the key company stories. Anthropic had a rough weekend — delayed IPO, weak 2027 ARR projections, and reports of enormous OpenAI cash burn with negative free cash flow of roughly 280 billion dollars expected through 2030. Oracle is also under pressure after a Financial Times report highlighted that efforts to offload loans tied to its massive New Mexico data center have hit a wall. These headlines are a headwind for the broader AI infrastructure trade, even though European data center names are holding up this morning.

Novo Nordisk fell in European trading after disappointing investors at its analyst day by failing to provide specific financial targets. Disney, by contrast, is getting positive press — its parks are outperforming industry peers by leaning into price promotions and package deals. And Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery remain in the news as Paramount is reportedly in advanced settlement talks with California over the Warner merger, potentially agreeing to preserve editorial independence at CNN and divest cable channels including Comedy Central.

The key catalysts to watch this week are the Trump and Xi summit on Thursday, any diplomatic signals out of the UN General Assembly, and the September flash PMIs on Wednesday morning. The bear case is real — geopolitics are genuinely dangerous, the Iran war is spreading, monetary policy globally is still tightening, and the US-China trade truce extension stalled over the weekend. But for today, the market is choosing hope over fear. Watch oil — that is the tell.
